Vendored fork of upstream fab_m3e 0.1.1. The patched source lives in this repo at packages/fab_m3e/lib/src/fab_menu_m3e.dart. The patch is activated by the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides path: entry — remove that entry and flutter pub get silently reverts to upstream.

Overview & role

fab_m3e is a leaf Material 3 Expressive UI widget package. Hexagonal / domain-layer concerns are N/A — it has no data, service, or routing surface. It only renders widgets and consumes m3e_design tokens.

This package is one of four vendored forks of EmilyMoonstone/material_3_expressive pinned in this repo (alongside navigation_rail_m3e, split_button_m3e, toolbar_m3e). Each fork exists because a specific upstream behaviour was wrong for this product; the patch is small and surgical.

What this is

A vendored fork of upstream fab_m3e 0.1.1. The fork is pulled in transitively via the m3e_collection umbrella package, and activated by a path: dependency_overrides entry in the root pubspec.yaml. The patched file is packages/fab_m3e/lib/src/fab_menu_m3e.dart. The patch marker in source is // Patched (vendored fork).

Glossary

  • Fork — a vendored copy of an upstream package, edited in-tree, pinned by a path: override.
  • Override — the dependency_overrides: block in the root pubspec.yaml that forces pub to resolve this package from a local folder instead of pub.dev.
  • Patch marker — an inline comment tag (// Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH) that flags every block of code changed from upstream. Audit with grep -rEn 'FORK|fork patch|PATCH|vendored' packages/fab_m3e/lib.
  • Re-sync — the procedure for re-applying this fork's patches onto a newer upstream version (see §9).
  • M3E — Material 3 Expressive, the motion/shape system this widget implements.

Architecture — the fork contract

The fork contract has two halves: WHY the patch exists (the root pubspec.yaml override comment) and HOW it is implemented (the inline // Patched (vendored fork) / // Fork patch: / // PATCH markers in lib/src/).

The fork contract (shared)

Every vendored fork in this repo carries the same contract:

  • The WHY is documented in the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides comment block above each path: entry. Read it before editing.
  • The HOW is flagged in source with // Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH. Every changed block has a marker.
  • The audit command is grep -rEn 'FORK|fork patch|PATCH|vendored' packages/<name>/lib — re-run after every edit and before every re-sync.
  • The doc-gap checklist (every fork carries this debt): add a > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner to the README; backfill the CHANGELOG; fix the EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).
  • The test contract: every fork SHOULD ship a test/. navigation_rail_m3e currently has NONE (highest debt); the other three forks do ship one.

Public API reference

The barrel lib/fab_m3e.dart exports five symbols. The fork only changes the internals of FabMenuM3E; the public signatures are unchanged from upstream.

FabMenuM3E

packages/fab_m3e/lib/src/fab_menu_m3e.dart

class FabMenuM3E extends StatefulWidget {
  const FabMenuM3E({
    required this.primaryFab,
    required this.items,
    this.direction = FabMenuDirection.up,
    this.spacing,
    this.overlay = true,
    this.alignment = Alignment.bottomRight,
    this.popOnItemTap = true,
    this.controller,
    this.heroTag,
  });

  final Widget primaryFab;
  final List<FabMenuItem> items;
  final FabMenuDirection direction;
  final FabMenuController? controller;
  // ... see source for the rest
}

class FabMenuItem {
  final Widget icon;
  final Widget label;
  final VoidCallback onPressed;
  final String? semanticLabel;
}

class FabMenuController extends ChangeNotifier {
  bool get isOpen;
  void open();
  void close();
  void toggle();
}
  • FabMenuM3E L1-13: StatefulWidget. The fork only changes the State's reveal animation; constructor signature is identical to upstream.
  • FabMenuDirection L15-17: Re-exported from enums.dart. Drives _originFor(direction) so each item scales from the corner facing the FAB.
  • FabMenuItem L25-30: Plain model: icon, label, onPressed, optional semanticLabel.
  • FabMenuController L32-37: External controller hook; open/close/toggle + isOpen. Optional — fork creates an internal one if omitted.

FabM3E / ExtendedFabM3E

FabM3E and ExtendedFabM3E (in src/fab_m3e.dart and src/extended_fab_m3e.dart) are unchanged from upstream. They take kind (FabM3EKind), size (FabM3ESize), density (FabM3EDensity), onPressed, and standard M3E token-driven styling. FabMenuM3E builds each menu item as an ExtendedFabM3E with kind: FabM3EKind.surface.

FabTokensAdapter

FabTokensAdapter (in src/fab_theme_m3e.dart, exported via show) bridges m3e_design tokens into FAB colors/shapes. Unpatched. Re-exported from the barrel as export 'src/fab_theme_m3e.dart' show FabTokensAdapter;.

Usage playbook

example/fab_menu_usage.dart

import 'package:m3e_collection/m3e_collection.dart';

FabMenuM3E(
  primaryFab: FabM3E(
    icon: const Icon(Icons.add),
    onPressed: () {},
  ),
  direction: FabMenuDirection.up,
  items: [
    FabMenuItem(icon: const Icon(Icons.note), label: const Text('Note'), onPressed: () {}),
    FabMenuItem(icon: const Icon(Icons.task), label: const Text('Task'), onPressed: () {}),
  ],
)
  • direction L5: Drives _originFor(): up=bottomRight, down=topRight, left=centerRight, right=centerLeft. Each item scales from that corner of its own box.
  • items L7-10: Reveal order = list order; the item nearest the FAB leads the stagger.

5b. Wiring — how a host actually gets this fork

pubspec.yaml (root)

# Vendored fork of fab_m3e 0.1.1 (pulled in transitively via m3e_collection).
# Patched so the FAB Menu reveals items with a staggered, FAB-anchored spring
# (M3E spec) instead of one center-origin scale+fade, and never draws a scrim.
# Source of the patch: packages/fab_m3e/lib/src/fab_menu_m3e.dart.
dependency_overrides:
  fab_m3e:
    path: packages/fab_m3e
  • WHY L1-4: Root pubspec.yaml override comment. This is the auditable reason for the fork; edit it whenever the patch changes.
  • HOW L5-7: path: override activates the fork. m3e_collection still re-exports fab_m3e by name; the override redirects that name to the local folder.

Hosts almost never import package:fab_m3e/... directly. The fork is pulled in transitively via m3e_collection (the umbrella that re-exports every M3E widget), and most apps reach it through arxa_kit's Kit* wrappers. The root dependency_overrides path: entry is the only thing that activates the patch — m3e_collection's own version constraint is unchanged.

Gotchas + re-sync procedure

The fork uses Interval.transform on the raw controller value instead of allocating a CurvedAnimation per item per build. Upstream's per-item CurvedAnimation allocation leaked in Flutter 3.44. Do not "simplify" the loop back to CurvedAnimation — that reintroduces the leak.

Forward duration is 300ms (raised from upstream's 200ms so the stagger cascade is legible). Reverse stays 200ms. If you change _staggerSpread, re-test with 4+ items — the cascade collapses if the spread window is too narrow.

Re-sync procedure (shared across all four forks)

When bumping upstream (fab_m3e, navigation_rail_m3e, split_button_m3e, or toolbar_m3e):

1. Bump the fork's pubspec.yaml version: and the root pubspec.yaml override comment's stated version. 2. Backfill the fork's CHANGELOG.md with the new version entry (every fork's CHANGELOG is stale — see §11). 3. Diff each patched file against the new upstream release of the same path. 4. Re-apply each // Patched (vendored fork) / // Fork patch: / // PATCH block by hand. Do NOT copy upstream over the fork blindly — the markers are your only map of what to preserve. 5. Update the root pubspec.yaml override comment if the WHY or the patched-file list changed. 6. Run the fork's flutter test in packages/<name>/, then run the consuming showcase (arxa_kit_showcase) to confirm the patched behaviour still renders.

Override hygiene (shared)

Never remove a dependency_overrides path: entry without first confirming upstream includes the fix. A "clean" flutter pub get silently reverts the fork to the pub.dev release, and the patch — including its bug fix — disappears with no compile error. The root override comment is the only durable record of why the patch exists.

Doc-gap debt every fork carries: (a) no > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner in the README; (b) stale CHANGELOG.md; (c) EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).

Decisions / ADRs

None. The fork contract is documented in the root pubspec.yaml override comment; no separate ADR was written. If the patch grows beyond one file, write one.
